issues.description: Class name mismatch for the core data type: the problem statement and solution describe and use a class named Meal with a constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters. The template repository instead provides an implemented Order class (Order(String, String[]), getName(), getIngredients()) and an empty Meal.java. This naming/identifier inconsistency means students will see different class names in the instructions and in the starter code (and Main in the template references Order). This prevents a straightforward implementation and may cause compile/runtime confusion when following examples or tests that expect Meal.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement and solution: provide a concrete Meal class in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java matching the solution (constructor Meal(String, String[]), getName(), getIngredients()). Remove or rename the Order class (or clearly document the intended name), and update the Main examples to reference Meal. Alternatively, rename Order.java to Meal.java in the template and ensure the file content and any references match the problem specification.

issues.description: The exercise describes and expects a class named 'Meal' (problem statement references a fully implemented Meal with getName/getIngredients), but the template repository provides an 'Order' class that has the same structure and responsibilities (name + ingredients) while Meal.java in the template is empty. The solution repository uses a class named 'Meal'. This inconsistent identifier mapping (Meal vs Order) means students cannot directly find or use the expected 'Meal' type in the starter code, increasing confusion and blocking straightforward implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the meal entity across artifacts. Recommended: rename the template's Order class to Meal (adjust the file name to Meal.java and class declaration to public class Meal) and update all template references (e.g., Main and any comments) to use Meal. Ensure the template's Meal.java contains the same constructor and getters as in the solution (private final String name; private final String[] ingredients; constructor Meal(String, String[]); getName(); getIngredients()). Alternatively, if Order is intentional, update the problem statement to consistently refer to 'Order' instead of 'Meal' and provide a clear note about the alias. Prefer keeping 'Meal' to match the solution and problem description.
